dedupe_keys.name: potential impacts of climate change on world food supply datasets from a major crop modelling study rosenzweig and iglesias nasa giss sedac

description: Projected country and regional changes in grain crop yields under climate change from the Rosenzweig and Iglesias crop modelling study, with knock-on effects on world food supply. The NASA Earthdata page says equilibrium and transient General Circulation Model scenarios, with three levels of farmer adaptation, were used to estimate yields of wheat, rice, coarse grains (barley and maize) and soybean at 125 agricultural sites in major world regions; the site results were aggregated to trading regions and fed into the Basic Linked System (BLS) global trade model to give potential price increases, food shortages and risk of hunger. The data were produced by the Goddard Institute for Space Studies and distributed by CIESIN through SEDAC as version 1.00 (1999), openly shared under the EOSDIS data use guidance and free after an Earthdata login; the geographic extent spans 58 degrees south to 90 degrees north. Caveats: the scenarios come from 1990s GCMs and should be read as a historical benchmark. For simulation it gives a classic coupled crop and trade experiment, useful for comparing newer food system shock models. Related catalogue records include the GGCMI crop model outputs and the ISIMIP data repository.
